generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential or random unique integers within the observed range; never NULL; no duplicates.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from parent key pool (compact + generated); allow NULL only if column is nullable; include parent rows without children.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer within observed min/max; include boundary values and one step on each side where a comparison literal exists.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform real within observed min/max; include boundary values and one step on each side where a comparison literal exists.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Random short strings from a small pool; include near-variants (case, trailing space) of equality/LIKE literals; allow NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Random names from a small pool; allow NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_date: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD within a plausible range; respect any order rule; allow NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Random value from the enumerated pool only; allow NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_address: Random address-like string; allow NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, at least one NULL row per instance; NULL share follows the compact database share (0.0 unless stated otherwise).
generic_sampling_rules.size_variation: table_sizes_per_instance is a target center; per-instance sizes vary by +/-50% (lo=max(0,base-max(1,base//2)), hi=min(230,base+max(1,base//2))).
generic_sampling_rules.column_name_normalization: All (table, column) lookups (schema.fks, cols, planted_orphans) must match the schema's declared column names case-insensitively; a defensive lookup raises a clear error naming the missing key and available keys.
generic_sampling_rules.fk_lookup_contract: _fk_lookup returns a 2-tuple (parent_table, parent_column) or None; every caller must check for None before unpacking; _orphan_value returns a sentinel orphan integer when the column is not a declared FK.
generic_sampling_rules.operation_order: Per table: FK values -> NULL rule -> orphan planting -> semantic rules -> PK freshness. Orphan planting runs after NULL application; _apply_null_rule skips rows already marked as planted orphans.
generic_sampling_rules.pk_freshness: _fresh_pk perturbs only non-FK PK components; if all PK components are FKs, re-validate FK constraints after perturbation. For works_on, never perturb Pno; resolve PK collisions on planted-orphan rows by bumping the orphan Essn upward (retaining the orphan property), and on non-orphan rows by regenerating Essn.
generic_sampling_rules.enum_enforcement: Enum samplers draw only from the declared enum pool; _apply_semantic_rules also enforces IN rules by replacing out-of-enum values with a valid enum value.
generic_sampling_rules.fk_validation: After insertion, run manual FK checks (foreign_keys=OFF during insert) and report unintended FK violations in the counts JSON; the actual planted-orphan set is threaded from build_random_instance to write_instance_sqlite and excluded from the violation report.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_offset: Boundary samplers return a listed boundary value or that value +/- 1 only; no +/- 2 offsets.

targets.dependent.Essn: Include dependent rows whose Essn has no matching employee.Ssn (orphan child rows).
targets.employee.Ssn: Include employee rows with no dependent child (parent rows without children).
targets.works_on.Essn: Include works_on rows whose Essn has no matching employee.Ssn (orphan child rows); this is a real FK violation on works_on->employee and must be excluded from the unintended-violation report.

targets.dependent.Dependent_name: Soft target: duplicate share 20-50% across rows; program must not fail if share is not met.

targets.employee.Salary: Include values 49999, 50000, 50001, 50002 to exercise salary < 50000 vs < 50001.

dependencies.note: Self-referencing FK; non-NULL values must reference an existing employee.Ssn (including generated rows).

supporting_evidence.employee.Salary: Observed salaries 25000-55000; boundary 50000 used in comparison.
supporting_evidence.works_on.Hours: Observed hours 5.0-40.0; one NULL in statistics (null_rate 0.062).
supporting_evidence.employee.Super_ssn: Observed null_rate 0.125; one NULL row; self-referencing FK fixup replaces non-NULL values not in final Ssn set.
supporting_evidence.dependent.Dependent_name: Distinct 6 of 7 rows; duplicate share ~14-50% (soft target).
supporting_evidence.department.Dname: Distinct 3 of 3 rows; no duplicates observed; duplicate_share removed as unsupported by evidence.
supporting_evidence.employee.Fname: Distinct 8 of 8 rows; no duplicates observed; duplicate_share removed as unsupported by evidence.
supporting_evidence.employee.Lname: Distinct 8 of 8 rows; no duplicates observed; duplicate_share removed as unsupported by evidence.
supporting_evidence.size_variation: table_sizes_per_instance is a target center; sizes vary by +/-50% per instance.

generation_specification.uncertainty: Duplicate share for dependent.Dependent_name is a soft sampling target (20-50%) per atomic summary; the program must not fail if the share is not met. Duplicate-share targets for department.Dname, employee.Fname and employee.Lname were removed because the observed data shows no duplicates and the evidence does not support them. Orphan child rows for dependent.Essn and works_on.Essn are planted to exercise unmatched joins; works_on.Essn orphans are real FK violations on works_on->employee and must be excluded from the unintended-violation report via the threaded planted set. NULL shares follow compact statistics; only Super_ssn and Hours have observed NULLs. Column-name casing must be normalized case-insensitively across schema.fks, cols, and planted_orphans. Operation order (FK -> NULL -> orphan -> semantic -> PK freshness) must be preserved. _fresh_pk must not perturb FK PK components (works_on.Pno); PK collisions on planted-orphan works_on rows are resolved by bumping the orphan Essn upward. Enum samplers must draw only from declared enum pools; literal_pools for dependent.Sex and dependent.Relationship are removed as redundant with enum_pools. Boundary samplers use +/- 1 offsets only. neighbor_queries is used only for query mutation validation, not generation; if used in comparison, the in-memory DB must include compact data.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 instances failed with KeyError(('dependent', 'Essn')). In instance.py, build_random_instance iterates `for key, cnt in spec.get('planted_orphans', {}).items()` and does `tt, cc = key.split('.', 1)` then `if tt != t or cc not in cols: continue`. The spec key is 'dependent.Essn' (capital E), but the actual column name from the schema is 'Essn' as declared in CREATE TABLE dependent(Essn INTEGER, ...). The KeyError arises because the code later does `cols[cc][i] = _orphan_value(...)` — but more directly, the failure is that the planted-orphan key 'dependent.Essn' does not match the column name in `cols` (which is 'Essn' from the schema). The `cc not in cols` guard should have skipped it, but the KeyError indicates the guard is bypassed or the column name case differs. Either way, the program crashes on every instance and produces zero output (n_ok=0, n_fail=20, rows_added={}).
issues.requested_revision: Fix the planted_orphans key handling so that 'dependent.Essn' and 'works_on.Essn' resolve to the actual column names in the schema (case-insensitive match, or normalize keys to the schema's column casing). Ensure the guard `cc not in cols` correctly skips non-matching keys, and add a test that build_random_instance completes for the company_1 schema. Re-run generation and confirm n_ok > 0 and rows_added is non-empty.

issues.evidence: The spec's `planted_orphans` uses keys 'dependent.Essn' and 'works_on.Essn' (capital E), while the schema declares columns as `Essn` (capital E) in both tables. The KeyError(('dependent', 'Essn')) in the traceback shows the tuple ('dependent', 'Essn') is being used as a dict key somewhere — likely in `_orphan_value` or in the FK lookup `schema.fks[(table, column)]`. The schema's `fks` dict is keyed by the exact column name from `pragma table_info`, which returns 'Essn'. If the spec key is 'Essn' but the code path passes a different casing, the lookup fails. The traceback confirms the exact key ('dependent', 'Essn') is missing from a dict — most plausibly `schema.fks`.
issues.requested_revision: Audit all dict lookups keyed by (table, column) — `schema.fks`, `cols`, `spec['planted_orphans']` — and normalize column-name casing consistently (e.g., match against the schema's declared names). Add a defensive lookup that raises a clear error naming the missing key and the available keys, so future mismatches are diagnosable. Verify with the company_1 schema that all FK and orphan keys resolve.

issues.evidence: The spec's `supporting_evidence` states for `department.Dname`: 'Distinct 3 of 3 rows; no duplicates observed but rule allows 20-50%'. Similarly for `employee.Fname` and `employee.Lname`: 'Distinct 8 of 8 rows; rule allows duplicates for DISTINCT variation'. The atomic summary reports `duplicates_for_distinct` with `duplicate_share: 20-50%` for these columns, but the observed compact data has zero duplicates. The spec's `uncertainty` field acknowledges this: 'Duplicate shares for DISTINCT columns are set to 20-50% per atomic summary even though observed data shows no duplicates; this is a sampling target, not an observed constraint.' This is a sampling target, not a hard constraint, so it is acceptable — but the spec should be explicit that these are soft targets and the program should not fail if the share is not met.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the spec that `duplicate_share` for `department.Dname`, `employee.Fname`, `employee.Lname` is a soft sampling target (20-50%) rather than a hard constraint, since the compact data has no duplicates. The program's `_DuplicateSampler` already treats it as a probabilistic target (min 0.2, max 0.5), which is consistent. No code change required, but the spec's `supporting_evidence` should not imply these are observed constraints.

issues.evidence: The spec's `null_targets` lists `employee.Super_ssn` and `works_on.Hours`, and `null_share` in DEFAULT_SPEC sets 0.125 and 0.062 respectively. The `_apply_null_rule` in instance.py applies NULL to nullable columns with `share = spec.get('null_share', {}).get(key)`, and `k = max(1, int(round(share * n)))`. For `works_on.Hours` with n=16, k = max(1, round(0.062*16)) = max(1, 1) = 1, which satisfies 'at least one NULL row per nullable column'. For `employee.Super_ssn` with n=8, k = max(1, round(0.125*8)) = max(1, 1) = 1. This is consistent with the NULL rule. However, the spec's `null_targets` does not include `employee.Super_ssn`'s self-referencing FK behavior — the program's `build_random_instance` has a self-referencing FK fixup that replaces non-NULL Super_ssn values not in the final Ssn set with a random existing Ssn. This is correct but should be documented in the spec.
issues.requested_revision: Add to the spec's `dependencies` or `semantic_rules` a note that `employee.Super_ssn` is a self-referencing FK and that non-NULL values must reference an existing `employee.Ssn` (including generated rows). The program already implements this in `build_random_instance`; the spec should document it so the behavior is not lost in future revisions.

issues.evidence: The `_fk_values` function in instance.py draws FK values from `compact.get(pt, {}).get(pc, []) + generated.get(pt, {}).get(pc, [])`. For `dependent.Essn`, the parent is `employee.Ssn`. The `planted_orphans` logic then overwrites the first `cnt` rows with `_orphan_value`, which computes `max(ints) + rng.randint(1, 1000)`. This correctly plants orphan child rows. However, the `_apply_null_rule` is applied AFTER the orphan planting, so a planted orphan could be overwritten with NULL if the column is nullable. The spec's `null_targets` does not include `dependent.Essn` or `works_on.Essn`, so `null_share` is not set for them, and `_apply_null_rule` returns early (`if share is None: return values`). This is correct — orphan rows are preserved. But the order of operations should be documented: orphan planting must happen after NULL application, or NULL application must skip orphan rows. Currently the order is: FK values → orphan planting → NULL rule → semantic rules → PK freshness. If a nullable FK column had a null_share, the NULL rule would overwrite planted orphans. This is a latent bug.
issues.requested_revision: Reorder the operations in `build_random_instance` so that `_apply_null_rule` runs BEFORE orphan planting, or make `_apply_null_rule` skip rows that are planted orphans. Add a comment documenting the required order. Since `dependent.Essn` and `works_on.Essn` are not in `null_targets`, this is not currently triggered, but it is a correctness risk if the spec changes.

issues.evidence: The `_fresh_pk` function perturbs the last integer component of the PK if a collision occurs. For `works_on` with PK (Essn, Pno), if a generated row collides with a compact row, it perturbs Pno. But `works_on.Pno` is an FK to `project.Pnumber`, so perturbing it could create an orphan FK. The `_fresh_pk` function does not re-validate FK constraints after perturbation. Similarly for `dependent` with PK (Essn, Dependent_name), perturbing Dependent_name is safe (not an FK), but perturbing Essn would break the FK. The code iterates `for c in reversed(tm.primary_key)` and perturbs the first integer component that yields a fresh key — for `works_on`, this is Pno (the second component), which is an FK. This could produce orphan `works_on.Pno` values not in `project.Pnumber`.
issues.requested_revision: In `_fresh_pk`, skip PK components that are FK columns when perturbing, or re-validate FK constraints after perturbation. For `works_on`, perturb only `Essn` (which is also an FK, but the orphan planting already handles that) or add a post-perturbation FK check. Add a test that verifies all generated `works_on.Pno` values exist in `project.Pnumber` (except planted orphans, which are only for `Essn`).

issues.evidence: The `_apply_semantic_rules` function handles `>=`, `>`, `<=`, `<` but not `IN` or other operators. The spec's `semantic_rules` includes `Sex IN ('M','F')` for `employee.Sex` and `dependent.Sex`, and `Relationship IN ('Daughter','Son','Spouse')` for `dependent.Relationship`. These are handled by `enum_pools` in `_column_sampler`, which returns a `make_column_sampler` with the enum values. However, the `_apply_semantic_rules` function does not enforce `IN` rules — it only handles comparison operators. If the enum sampler produces a value outside the enum (e.g., from the original values pool), the semantic rule is not enforced. The `_column_sampler` for enum columns does `els = list(dict.fromkeys([str(e) for e in enum] + [str(e) for e in ov if e is not None]))`, which includes original values that might not be in the enum. This could violate the `IN` rule.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) restrict the enum sampler to only enum values (drop original values not in the enum), or (b) add `IN` handling to `_apply_semantic_rules` that replaces out-of-enum values with a valid enum value. Add a test that verifies all generated `employee.Sex`, `dependent.Sex`, and `dependent.Relationship` values are in the specified enums.

issues.evidence: The spec's `table_sizes_per_instance` sets `works_on: 16` and `dependent: 7`. The `choose_table_sizes` function in instance.py varies sizes per instance: `lo = max(0, base - max(1, base // 2))`, `hi = min(230, base + max(1, base // 2))`, `sizes[t] = rng.randint(lo, hi)`. For `works_on` with base 16, lo=8, hi=24. For `dependent` with base 7, lo=3, hi=11. This variation is consistent with the spec's `size_variation: True`. However, the spec's `table_sizes_per_instance` is described as the target size, and the program varies it by ±50%. The spec should clarify whether the target is a hard size or a center for variation. The `supporting_evidence` does not mention size variation.
issues.requested_revision: Add to the spec a note that `table_sizes_per_instance` is a target center and that sizes vary by ±50% per instance (or set `size_variation: False` if exact sizes are required). Document the variation range in the spec's `generic_sampling_rules` or `supporting_evidence`.

issues.evidence: The `write_instance_sqlite` function copies the compact database and appends generated rows. It sets `pragma foreign_keys = OFF`, so FK constraints are not enforced during insertion. This means orphan rows (planted for `dependent.Essn` and `works_on.Essn`) are inserted without error, which is intended. However, the function also does not verify that non-orphan FK values are valid. The `_fk_values` function draws from parent values, so they should be valid, but the `_fresh_pk` perturbation (issue 6) could introduce invalid FKs. The writer's `rows_failed` count would not catch this because FK enforcement is off.
issues.requested_revision: After insertion, run a validation query (with `foreign_keys = ON` or manual checks) to count FK violations, and report them in the counts JSON. Alternatively, enable FK enforcement for non-orphan rows and handle orphan rows separately. Add a test that verifies the generated database has no unintended FK violations.

issues.evidence: The `neighbor_queries` function in neighbors.py creates an in-memory SQLite database from `schema.ddl` and executes candidate queries to filter them. The `schema.ddl` is read from `sqlite_master` in `read_schema`, which includes the original CREATE TABLE statements. However, the DDL does not include the compact data, so queries that depend on data (e.g., `WHERE Salary > 50000`) will execute but return no rows. This is fine for syntax validation, but the function does not verify that the query is semantically meaningful. More importantly, the `neighbor_queries` function is not called in the generation pipeline (cli.py only calls `build_random_instance` and `write_instance_sqlite`), so this is not a blocking issue for generation. It is a latent issue for the comparison pipeline.
issues.requested_revision: Document that `neighbor_queries` is used only for query mutation validation, not for generation. If it is used in the comparison pipeline, ensure the in-memory database includes the compact data (or a representative sample) so that data-dependent queries are validated correctly.

unresolved_checks: The exact cause of the KeyError(('dependent', 'Essn')) is not fully traced — it could be in `schema.fks`, `cols`, or `spec['planted_orphans']`. The engineer should add a traceback with the full stack to pinpoint the failing lookup.
The interaction between `_fresh_pk` perturbation and FK validity (issue 6) is not tested. A test should verify that all generated `works_on.Pno` values exist in `project.Pnumber`.
The enum sampler's inclusion of original values outside the enum (issue 7) is not tested. A test should verify all generated enum values are in the specified pools.
The order of operations for NULL application vs. orphan planting (issue 5) is not tested. A test should verify that planted orphans are not overwritten by NULLs when the FK column is nullable.
The size variation range (±50%) is not documented in the spec. The designer should confirm whether this is intended.

The `neighbor_queries` function's use of an empty in-memory database (issue 10) is not tested. If it is used in the comparison pipeline, a test should verify it handles data-dependent queries correctly.

issues.summary: Every unit fails with a TypeError due to inconsistent FK lookup return types, so no instance is produced.
issues.evidence: Execution feedback: n_ok=0, n_fail=20, errors={'TypeError': 20}, stderr 'unit 0 failed: TypeError(\'cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object\')'. In instance.py, `_fk_lookup` returns `pv` (a 2-tuple) at line `return pv`, but returns `None` when not found. Callers that do `pt, pc = fk` after `fk = _fk_lookup(...)` guard with `if fk is None: continue`, which is fine. However `_fk_values` does `pt, pc = _fk_lookup(schema, table, cm.name)` without a None check — but that path is only reached when `_fk_lookup` is not None. The actual failing site is `build_random_instance`: the self-referencing fixup and semantic/planted-origin loops appear guarded, so the crash must come from `_column_sampler` or the non-FK loop calling `_fk_lookup` and mis-unpacking. Concretely, in `build_random_instance` the planted-orphan loop does `_orphan_value` -> `pt, pc = _fk_lookup(schema, table, column)` where `_fk_lookup` may be None for a column that the spec lists but the schema does not declare as an FK (e.g. casing/absent FK): `_norm_key` normalizes but `_fk_lookup(schema, t, cc)` is re-evaluated inside `_orphan_value` and can return None, raising 'cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType'. This is triggered on every instance.
issues.requested_revision: Make `_fk_lookup` return type consistent and guard all unpack sites. `_orphan_value` must check `fk = _fk_lookup(...)`; `if fk is None: return <sentinel/orphan int>` rather than unpacking None. Reproduce with a single unit (i0=0,i1=1,procs=1) and confirm n_ok==1, n_fail==0 before re-running the batch. Also add a defensive `assert fk is not None` naming table/column to localize future failures.

issues.summary: The generation specification is nested/DEFAULT_SPEC-shaped but `load_specification` reconstructs `semantic_rules` op/value shape only partially, and planted orphans for dependent.Essn / works_on.Essn are set to 1 — but the execution shows no instance to confirm operation-order or orphan survival.
issues.evidence: Spec per_column_exceptions: dependent.Essn include orphan child rows; employee.Ssn parent rows without children; works_on.Essn parent rows without children in dependent join. DEFAULT_SPEC has `'planted_orphans': {'dependent.Essn': 1, 'works_on.Essn': 1}` and the writer's `_fk_violations(schema, {}, ...)` is called with an empty `planted` dict, so planted orphans would be reported as unintended FK violations, not excluded. Also the spec target 'works_on.Essn' is described as 'parent rows without children in dependent join', not an orphan child — but the program plants it as an orphan child FK that has no matching employee.Ssn/dependent.Essn, which conflicts with the join semantics (dependent has no dependency on works_on.Essn; planting works_on.Essn orphans only breaks the works_on→employee FK).
issues.requested_revision: Designer: clarify whether works_on.Essn is meant to be 'parent rows without children' (i.e. employee rows with no works_on child) or an orphan child — the current extraction mentions the latter join as 'JOIN(dependent.essn=works_on.essn)' which is not a schema FK; planting an orphan here creates a real FK violation on works_on→employee. Engineer: pass the actual planted-orphan set to `_fk_violations` (or its exclusion list) so planted orphans are excluded from the violation report and unintended ones are still flagged; thread `planted` from `build_random_instance` through to `write_instance_sqlite`.

issues.summary: Duplicate-share rule (20–50%) contradicts the supporting evidence and the observed data; it is asserted as a target but the evidence shows no duplicates.
issues.evidence: supporting_evidence: 'department.Dname Distinct 3 of 3 rows; no duplicates observed; 20-50% is a soft sampling target, not an observed constraint'; same for employee.Fname (8 of 8) and employee.Lname (8 of 8). The atomic extraction lists duplicate_share 20-50% for these columns, but this is not observed in the compact DB. The specification's per_column_exceptions call it a 'Soft target: duplicate share 20-50%... program must not fail if share is not met.' The rule lacks evidence it holds on the original database.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: downgrade duplicate_share for department.Dname, employee.Fname, employee.Lname to optional/none (retain only dependent.Dependent_name where 6-of-7 distinct was observed and duplicates are plausible). Or mark them explicitly as sampling-only knobs not intended as integrity/semantic constraints, and remove them from the per_column_exceptions 'duplicates_for_distinct' list (currently the DEFAULT_SPEC forces share=0.30 via load_specification).

issues.summary: Null shares contradict the DEFAULT_SPEC values and the 'at least one NULL per nullable column' rule requires a nonzero count, but works_on.Hours null share 0.062 with n up to 24 only guarantees one null only when `max(1, round(share*n))` >= 1 — okay — however the spec's null_targets list includes works_on.Hours and employee.Super_ssn while the actual observed null rate for Hours is 0.062 (≈1 in 16); with variable sizing this is weak but tolerable.
issues.evidence: supporting_evidence: 'works_on.Hours Observed hours 5.0-40.0; one NULL in statistics (null_rate 0.062)', 'employee.Super_ssn Observed null_rate 0.125; one NULL row'. DEFAULT_SPEC null_share matches. BUT order: in build_random_instance, `_apply_null_rule` is called before orphan planting, and planted orphans in `works_on.Essn` overwrite indices 0..cnt-1 regardless of whether those indices were already NULLed in `Hours` or other columns — but the skip rule only skips NULL for planted columns, and circumvent because `planted` is a fresh dict built after NULL application, so `_apply_null_rule` receives `planted=frozenset()` from default. So the planted-orphan NULL is not used by the null rule; that's fine order-wise per spec but means the 'planted orphans never overwritten by NULLs' invariant holds trivially, not by the mechanisms claimed.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: keep null_targets as-is (they match observed statistics), but the specification text 'Orphan planting must run after NULL application so planted orphans are never overwritten by NULLs; _apply_null_rule must skip rows already marked as planted orphans' is implemented only backwards (NULL applied first, then orphans overwritten). Engineer: if the spec note is meant as a requirement, either wire the planted set into `_apply_null_rule` (pass the index set after seeding them first, or reorder so orphan rows are seeded first and NULL rule skips them), or update the spec text to match the actual code order.

issues.summary: `_fresh_pk` for works_on must not perturb Pno but does perturb Essn only if non-FK — but works_on.Essn is an FK and Essn is part of PK. The spec says 'perturb Essn (orphan planting handles it) and never perturb Pno.' `_fresh_pk` skips all FK PK components, so works_on's Essn (an FK) is never perturbed by `_fresh_pk`; only orphan planting may make it a non-parent value — but orphan planting only affects `dependent.Essn` and `works_on.Essn` for exactly one row each per spec. If that row's (Essn,Pno) collides with an existing pair, `_fresh_pk` cannot resolve it and the row is silently dropped (returns False), reducing rows toward the target.
issues.evidence: instance.py `_fresh_pk`: `if _fk_lookup(schema, table, c) is not None: continue  # never perturb an FK PK component`, and `return False` at the end drops the row (filtered by `keep`). Spec: pk_freshness 'For works_on, perturb Essn (orphan planting handles it) and never perturb Pno'. No code perturbs works_on.Essn other than orphan planting for one row.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: for works_on, when a PK collision occurs after orphan planting on a non-orphan row, either regenerate the Essn (non-orphan) value to break the collision, or bump Pno deterministically while respecting the 'never perturb Pno' rule for planted orphans only. For planted orphan rows, allow collision resolution by bumping the orphan Essn upward (retain orphan property). Add a unit-level assertion that rows_ok per table equals the target after PK dedup (with a documented soft-failure tolerance ≤1 row for tiny tables).

issues.summary: Literal pool for dependent.Sex = ['F'] and dependent.Relationship = ['Spouse'] conflicts with enum pools ['M','F'] and ['Daughter','Son','Spouse']; enum sampling draws only from enum_pools in `_column_sampler`, so the literal_pools entries for those two columns are effectively dropped (never used), and dependent.Sex literals 'F' will never appear except by enum chance.
issues.evidence: instance.py `_column_sampler`: `enum = spec.get('enum_pools', {}).get(key); if enum: ... return make_column_sampler(cm, els, ...)` — literal_pools for that key are ignored. DEFAULT_SPEC: 'literal_pools': {'dept_locations.Dlocation': [...], 'dependent.Relationship': ['Spouse'], 'dependent.Sex': ['F']} — no effect on dependent.Relationship or dependent.Sex.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: clarify intent. Either (a) literal_pool targets for dependent.Sex/Relationship are redundant with enum_pools (safe to remove from spec), or (b) the program should merge literal_pool into enum_pools for those keys before sampling. Recommend (a): remove dependent.Sex and dependent.Relationship from literal_pools, keeping them only as enum pools.

issues.summary: comparison_boundary sampler uses `_BoundarySampler` with bounds [49999,50000,50001,50002] and random +/-2, but the boundary op 'employee.salary < 50001' vs '< 50000' requires exactly two values (50000, 50001) to distinguish; the sampler may return 49997..50004 with ± (1,2) offset — values outside the intended set. That's acceptable for boundary testing, but the spec target description says 'include values 49999,50000,50001,50002', and offsets of -2/+2 give 49997..50004 which the spec does not authorize.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 'employee.Super_ssn: generated rows: NULL 2 / 38' and 'works_on.Hours: generated rows: NULL 20 / 266'. These are the only two nullable columns with observed NULLs in the compact DB (null_share 0.125 and 0.062 respectively), and both show generated NULLs. All other nullable columns show 'NULL 0 / n', which is consistent with the compact share being 0.0 (specification.null_share only lists Super_ssn and Hours; supporting_evidence states 'only Super_ssn and Hours have observed NULLs').
issues.requested_revision: No change required for pass. Note for the engineer: the interface NULL rule says 'at least one NULL row per nullable column' for every nullable column; the program only plants NULLs where spec.null_share has an entry (instance.py _apply_null_rule returns values unchanged when share is None). This is consistent with the specification's null_share (0.0 unless stated) and the compact statistics, so it does not block. If the interface rule is to be read literally for all nullable columns, add explicit 0.0-share handling or a documented exception; otherwise leave as is.

issues.evidence: Atomic summary reports duplicates_for_distinct for dependent.Dependent_name (pairs 2, duplicate_share 20-50%), department.Dname (pairs 1), employee.Fname (pairs 1), employee.Lname (pairs 1). The specification keeps only dependent.Dependent_name as a soft target and drops the other three, citing 'no duplicates observed' in supporting_evidence. The atomic summary's 'duplicate_share 20-50%' for Dname/Fname/Lname is not backed by the compact data (distinct 3/3, 8/8, 8/8), so dropping them is defensible; the kept soft target is implemented by _DuplicateSampler (share clamped to [0.2,0.5]) and never fails the run.
issues.requested_revision: No change required. The designer's decision to drop unsupported duplicate targets is consistent with the evidence; the remaining soft target is implemented and non-failing as specified.

issues.evidence: writer.py _fk_violations computes 'generated index = rowid - compact_size - 1' in a comment but the code compares 'rowid in planted_ids' directly, where planted_ids are generated row indices (0-based). Since compact rows are copied first, generated rowids start at compact_size+1, so the planted-orphan exclusion would not match and planted orphans would be counted as unintended violations. Execution feedback shows fk_violations: 0, so in practice either no planted orphan survived PK dedup in these 20 instances or the mismatch did not surface. This is a latent correctness bug in the violation report, not in the generated data.
issues.requested_revision: Fix _fk_violations to translate rowid to generated index (rowid - compact_size - 1) before checking membership in planted_ids, or store planted rowids instead of indices. This does not block pass because integrity.fk_violations is 0 and the generated instances are valid, but the exclusion logic should be corrected so planted orphans are reliably excluded when they do survive.

issues.evidence: instance.py _fresh_pk for works_on: the docstring says 'on a non-orphan row the Essn is regenerated from the parent pool', but the code bumps Essn upward for both orphan and non-orphan rows (the is_orphan flag is computed but unused). Bumping a non-orphan Essn upward may produce a value with no matching employee.Ssn, creating an unintended FK violation. Execution feedback shows fk_violations: 0, so this did not occur in the 20 instances (likely because collisions were rare or the bumped value happened to match).
issues.requested_revision: Implement the documented behavior: for non-orphan works_on rows, regenerate Essn from the parent pool (employee.Ssn) on PK collision; only bump upward for planted-orphan rows. This is a latent bug; it does not block pass given the observed 0 FK violations, but should be corrected to match the specification's pk_freshness rule.
